scope: Authored active documentation and UI; substantive sources in retained dated research notes. Screening-only search hits and inherited Microsoft-template tutorials are historical material, not scientific citations supporting this project.
limits: This is a targeted reference and editorial audit, not an exhaustive systematic review.
Current access levels are recorded per source. Historical search logs and their access descriptions are preserved.
Official software feature pages are descriptions, not independent evidence of efficacy.

references.title: Systematic reviewers used various approaches to data extraction and expressed several research needs: a survey.
supported_claims: In a self-selected survey of 162 reviewers, spreadsheets and adapted extraction forms were common.
limitations: Current appraisal used the PubMed abstract, not the full article or supplements.
Survey responses do not represent all review teams.

references.title: Effects of double data extraction on errors in evidence synthesis: a crossover, multicenter, investigator-blinded, randomized controlled trial.
supported_claims: Cross-checking reduced but did not eliminate errors in the tested binary adverse-outcome extraction task.
limitations: Current appraisal used the PubMed abstract, not the full article or supplements.
100 participants; study-level and cell-level error rates have different denominators. No universal error rate follows.

references.title: Data extraction and comparison for complex systematic reviews: a step-by-step guideline and an implementation example using open-source software.
references.authors: Mohamed Afifi, Henrik Stryhn, Javier Sanchez
supported_claims: The authors describe a structured extraction, comparison and adjudication workflow with Epi Info and R.
limitations: Current appraisal used the PubMed abstract, not the full article or supplements.
Methods proposal and worked implementation, not an effectiveness trial of EvidenceTrail.

references.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Data Extraction With a Large Language Model: A Study Within Reviews.
supported_claims: The evaluated AI-assisted workflow retained human verification; omissions remained an error category.
limitations: Current appraisal used the PubMed abstract, not the full article or supplements.
Six reviews, 63 studies and particular models; shared errors may escape disagreement-only adjudication. Historical review records its own access level.

references.title: Data extraction by generative artificial intelligence: Assessing determinants of accuracy using human-extracted data from systematic review databases.
supported_claims: Accuracy varied by extraction variable; detailed definitions were associated with higher accuracy.
limitations: Current appraisal used the PubMed abstract, not the full article or supplements.
Association is not a causal test of this interface; reference data were human-extracted.

references.title: Performance of two large language models for data extraction in evidence synthesis.
supported_claims: PDF parsing and the supplied input affected extraction results in a ten-article model comparison.
limitations: Current appraisal used the PubMed abstract, not the full article or supplements.
Small historical model comparison; training-data overlap was unknown.

references.title: Automating the data extraction process for systematic reviews using GPT-4o and o3.
supported_claims: Performance varied with variable type and evaluation dataset.
limitations: Current appraisal used the PubMed abstract, not the full article or supplements.
Small later evaluations; external-set performance after method adjustment is not an untouched external test. Historical partial full-text access is preserved separately.

references.title: Chapter 5: Collecting data
references.authors: Li T, Higgins JPT, Deeks JJ
supported_claims: Studies and reports are distinct; extraction should retain their relationships.
Structured, piloted forms and planned handling of disagreements support transparent extraction.
limitations: Chapter last updated October 2019; handbook citation is version 6.5 (2024). Guidance does not evaluate either project.

references.title: Chapter 14: Completing Summary of findings tables and grading the certainty of the evidence
supported_claims: GRADE evaluates certainty by outcome across a body of evidence; populated cells do not establish certainty.
limitations: Chapter last updated August 2023; guidance is for intervention evidence, not a software quality score.

references.title: JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis
references.authors: Aromataris E, Lockwood C, Porritt K, Pilla B, Jordan Z, editors
supported_claims: Section 10.2.7 recommends trying scoping-review charting forms on two or three sources with at least two team members; transparent alternatives may be considered.
limitations: March 2024 PDF, printed page 170 (zero-based PDF page 169); later online chapter numbering differs. Only relevant sections were inspected.

references.title: How to do comparison and consensus in Extraction 1
supported_claims: Documents dual-reviewer comparison and consensus handling.
limitations: Product documentation, not comparative effectiveness evidence.

references.title: How to do comparison and consensus in Extraction 2
supported_claims: Documents separate reviewer forms, conflict display and final decisions.
limitations: Product documentation; both reviewers leaving a field blank does not raise a conflict.

references.title: REDCap software
supported_claims: REDCap supports data dictionaries, online surveys and databases.
limitations: Feature descriptions are vendor documentation, not evidence of benefit from EvidenceTrail.

references.title: Epi Info product notice
references.authors: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
supported_claims: CDC reports that Epi Info product development and technical assistance ended in September 2025.
limitations: Historical methods example is retained; this is not a current support recommendation.
corrections: Added current support-status context to the retained historical comparison.

references.title: ASReview LAB repository
supported_claims: The project implements model-assisted prioritization using human screening labels.
limitations: Repository README advertised version 3 when checked; the cited 2025 paper evaluates version 2. No code or performance is transferred to these projects.

references.title: revtools: Tools to support research synthesis in R
supported_claims: Repository identifies the project as research-synthesis tools in R.
limitations: Repository body did not expose detailed feature documentation in this retrieval; detailed import/screening claims are therefore not retained as verified current features.

references.title: RevMan
supported_claims: Cochrane describes study-data management, analysis and reporting features.
limitations: Product description does not establish comparative effectiveness.
corrections: Replaced the redirected legacy features URL with its current canonical destination.

references.title: The BagIt File Packaging Format (V1.0)
references.authors: Kunze J, Littman J, Madden E, Scancella J, Adams C
supported_claims: Manifests support checking payload integrity; section 5.4 explicitly excludes protection against active attacks.
limitations: Informational specification; EvidenceTrail uses a custom manifest and does not implement BagIt.

references.title: hashlib — Secure hashes and message digests
supported_claims: SHA-256 hashes byte inputs and can emit hexadecimal digests.
limitations: Hashing is not encryption, authentication or scientific validation.

references.title: What is GitHub Pages?
supported_claims: GitHub Pages logs visitor IP addresses even without sign-in.
limitations: Selected table contents staying in browser memory does not mean the host receives no page requests.

references.title: Configuring a publishing source for your GitHub Pages site
supported_claims: Pages supports branch publishing from the root or docs folder.
limitations: Instructions depend on repository permissions and settings; no deployment was performed in this review.
